visualReview.notes: Actually inspected90 final image pixels:13 portable,13 shared-material,29 medium-fi lighting/LOD and35 normal-placement terrain views. Five HES photographs and three guide illustrations/photographs were inspected as primary visual references. The ochre Hall, crow steps, palace/Lion’s Den, Chapel, King’s Old Building and low Forework remain legible. Original master is preserved; independent derivative fits lower gates and bailey to retained diagnostic LiDAR. New Port now faces the mapped front plane. All three Forework passages, north gate and New Port are genuine holes, with graded paving beyond the main Forework opening instead of the old tall terrace step. The Hall covered bridge has a reconstructed pointed underside and three opaque pointed reserves. Photographic dimensions and ornament remain approximations. Flat shared views expose buried terraces; terrain approval uses the separate normal-placement fixture. The old elevated gate camera and ancillary-obscured New Port camera do not establish clearance; dedicated grade images and rays do.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: All13 final shared-material pixels inspected. Three reusable graphs supply sandstone, lime plaster and slate, with visible common stone courses/roof pattern. Local opaque PBR supplies glazing and dark reserves. Skyline bakes actual common linear means into one draw. Each graph loads once in the production library. No embedded images or per-model photographic textures. The schematic flat-ground view exposes normally buried masonry; it does not establish site contact. Colors and texture scale are a shared stylization, not photographic matching.

Skyline ancillary roofs are bounded block silhouettes; later levels use mapped roof footprints. Strict style audit has zero findings. All levels satisfy1000/4000/16000/64000 triangles and1/4/4/4 draws. Terrain screenshots are diagnostic context, not accurate surrounding vegetation or town buildings.
